name: Operations
description: Rollout, service levels, latency, errors, incidents, alerting and running cost. Measured: an estimated concurrent-user ceiling and the business-case limitations of the feature as built.

fields.label: Environment
fields.description: Where it runs. The lens applies to what runs in production.

fields.label: Rollout
fields.description: Share of production traffic that has it. 100 when it is in production without a flag.

fields.label: Capacity (estimate)
fields.description: An estimate, not a load test: how many people could use the feature at the same time, as built, before it fails or degrades badly. The evidence names the bottleneck.

fields.label: Limitations
fields.description: Business cases a customer or operator would expect the feature to handle that it cannot, as built.

scan.instructions: Judge one feature at a time from its code (the files of its contexts and its evidence in the map), its configuration and its deployment files. A feature with no runtime of its own (documentation, build scripts, developer tooling) gets no readings: mark it not applicable with the reason. capacityUsers is an estimate, not a load test: how many people could use the feature at the same time, as built, before it fails or degrades badly. Read its concurrency model (one process or thread, async I/O, worker pools), its storage (a local file or embedded database, connection pools, locks, single-writer designs), the external services it calls and their rate limits or quotas, in-memory state that cannot be shared across instances, and single-actor designs (one desktop window, one command-line session). The ceiling is the tightest of these. Give one integer, rounded to a plausible order of magnitude (1, 10, 50, 100, 1000 and so on) and never more precise than the code supports; the first evidence line names that bottleneck with file:line, the next lines the next tightest. A desktop or command-line app one person runs answers honestly: 1, with that reason. limitations: count business-case limitations of the feature as built, things a customer or operator would reasonably expect it to do that it cannot (one account only, one currency, no undo, no export, no retry after a failed payment, a hard size cap); the evidence lists one short line per limitation with file:line. The capacity ceiling is not counted again as a limitation. Each reading is one integer; 0 is a reading only when you looked and found none.
